## Findings
- claim-1: The primary source states that \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) is generated as an ideal of \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) by \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\). [source-2@L1365-L1375|claim=formal-document]
- claim-2: **Conditional presentation-and-Pieri certificate.** Assume the integral interval presentation for \(p=c=1\), namely \(q=i+1\), \(r=j+1\), \(d=ij\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), and \[ M_{d+k}=\bigoplus_{\substack{i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i+1)^{j+1}\\|\mu|=d+k}}\mathbb Zs_\mu \quad(0\le k\le b), \] with complete \(h_1\)-row set \[ \{h_1s_\lambda:i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq(i+1)^{j+1},\ |\lambda|=d+k-1\}. \] Then, for \(1\le k\le b\), putting \[ P_{x,y}:=s_{((i+1)^x,i^{\,j-x},y)} \quad(y=0\text{ omitted}), \] one has \[ M_{d+k}=\bigoplus_{x=0}^{k}\mathbb ZP_{x,k-x}, \] and its complete \(h_1\)-row set is precisely \[ h_1P_{x,k-1-x}=P_{x+1,k-1-x}+P_{x,k-x} \qquad(0\le x\le k-1). \] Thus the row lattice is \[ L_k=\sum_{x=0}^{k-1}\mathbb Z(C_x+C_{x+1}),\qquad C_x=P_{x,k-x}. \] Deleting \(C_0\), respectively \(C_k\), gives lower-, respectively upper-, unitriangular \(k\times k\) matrices, both of determinant \(1\). For \(k=0\), \(M_d=\mathbb Zs_{i^j}\), the row set is empty, and the empty complementary determinant is \(1\).
## Strategy
Invoke the following presentation hypothesis for \(i,j\ge1\), \(d=ij\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), \(q=i+1\), \(r=j+1\):
\[
M_{d+k}=\bigoplus_{\substack{i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i+1)^{j+1}\\|\mu|=d+k}}\mathbb Zs_\mu,
\]
and its complete \(h_1\)-row set is
\[
\{h_1s_\lambda:\ i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq(i+1)^{j+1},\
|\lambda|=d+k-1\}.
\]

For \(0\le k\le b\), every such \(\mu\) is uniquely
\[
P_{x,k-x}:=s_{((i+1)^x,i^{\,j-x},\,k-x)},\qquad 0\le x\le k,
\]
with a zero final part omitted. Indeed, its first \(j\) parts are \(i\) or \(i+1\), the latter occupy an initial block of length \(x\), and its sole possible extra part is \(k-x\). Conversely, \(x\le k\le j\) and \(k-x\le k\le i\), so every displayed partition is in the box.

For \(1\le k\le b\), the row indices are exactly
\[
P_{x,k-1-x},\qquad 0\le x\le k-1.
\]
Write \(y=k-1-x\). The in-box addable boxes are precisely:

1. Extend the first row of length \(i\), producing
\[
P_{x+1,y};
\]
this is in-box since \(x+1\le k\le j\).

2. Extend the last part \(y\), or append a new row if \(y=0\), producing
\[
P_{x,y+1};
\]
this is in-box since \(y+1=k-x\le k\le i\).

All other addable boxes are out-of-box: extending a row of length \(i+1\) gives width \(i+2\), while appending a further row when \(y>0\) gives \(j+2\) rows. Additions within a constant block other than its first row do not produce partitions. Hence
\[
h_1P_{x,k-1-x}=P_{x+1,k-1-x}+P_{x,k-x}.
\]

With \(C_x=P_{x,k-x}\), the row lattice is
\[
L_k=\sum_{x=0}^{k-1}\mathbb Z(C_x+C_{x+1}).
\]
Deleting \(C_0\) gives a lower unitriangular \(k\times k\) matrix; deleting \(C_k\) gives an upper unitriangular one. Both determinants are \(1\). For \(k=0\), \(M_d=\mathbb Zs_{i^j}\), the row set is empty, and the empty determinant is \(1\).

Thus the named certificate is established conditional on the explicitly invoked presentation and row-completeness hypotheses.

## Gaps
The direct-sum interval presentation and completeness of the \(h_1\)-row set are invoked, not independently proved or source-grounded here.

## Next
An unconditional version requires a separate proof or stable source grounding of those presentation hypotheses.
